blocker.summary: The user explicitly approved spending a Xenia/ReXGlue oracle session to extend PinnedShaderRuntime's pinned shader registry (271 variants, r456) -- the sole remaining rejection reason after the r457-r462 mechanical-fix chain. r463 attempted this and could not start: build/ntsc-uj/manifest.json and static-validation.json are a SHARED path between the 'native' and 'rexglue-oracle' build profiles (tools/build.py and tools/prepare.py both write to build/<target>/manifest.json, no per-profile subdirectory), and a later 'native' profile prepare/build (2026-08-30 21:13-21:17, the one this whole r399-r462 session depends on) overwrote the 'rexglue-oracle' profile's manifest that had been used to compile the already-built oracle binary at build/ntsc-uj/cmake/ac6recomp (2026-08-30 13:24). tools/run_gate.py (the only oracle runner correctly gated to the qualified XEX 6eefba42..., confirmed by direct sha256sum of /fastdata/.../.tools/ac6-recomp-us-assets-20260813/default.xex) refuses to start against the wrong-schema manifest. No destructive action was taken (no forced git stash/checkout on the submodule, no manual bypass of run_gate.py's checks) -- deciding that backlog's fate is explicitly left to the user, not taken unilaterally. Full state restored: nothing was actually written under build/ntsc-uj/ (verified by diff against a pre-attempt backup), the empty artifacts/ output directory created was removed. Named for r464: user decision on the AC6_recomp submodule's uncommitted backlog (commit as-is, isolate, or another option) -- without it, the oracle campaign to extend shader registry coverage remains open but not actionable. Still open, non-blocking: once the native wiring (r454-r462) is judged mature, reconsider its own, unrelated backlog commit decision; update tools/prepare.py/build.py to default to the current ISO path (convenience only).
